standardsRefs: Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can complete a realistic inventory and restocking task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.
scenario: Following a worked example, the learner picks one shared-space category, the pantry shelf, the bathroom toiletries, or the under-sink cleaning supplies, and physically checks what's actually there, comparing it against a simple low, adequate, or full rule to flag what needs restocking.
safetyNotes: If your inventory includes cleaning supplies, check labels without opening or mixing any containers — closed-container counting only.
If you notice any expired food or medicine while inventorying the pantry, tell a trusted adult rather than throwing it away yourself.

simulationAlternative.description: If a real shared space isn't available to inventory, use the sample pantry/toiletry list provided on this task sheet instead, applying the same low/adequate/full rule to the sample quantities given.

materials: adult-or-local: access to one shared household storage area (pantry shelf, toiletries cabinet, or cleaning supply area) to look at directly

tasks.directions: Analyze the complete worked example on swk-rfl-g8-u02-l02-model-card before beginning.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Complete the fictional coached case on swk-rfl-g8-u02-l02-guided-card, use criterion-specific feedback, and finish its fresh correction turn.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Choose the permitted real-life route or complete fictional route on swk-rfl-g8-u02-l02-independent-card; follow every step and retain only the named minimal evidence.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Complete the minimal evidence record on swk-rfl-g8-u02-l02-evidence-record; omit or fictionalize private details.

prompts.text: Was the low/adequate/full rule easy to apply to every item, or did any item not fit neatly into one category? Explain.

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g8-u02-l02-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g8-u02-l02-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g8-u02-l02-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Inventory accuracy: Lists at least six real items with quantities and a low/adequate/full label applied consistently using the stated rule. | Restock reasoning: Names two items to restock first with a specific, plausible reason for the priority order. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g8-u02-l02-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner design a restock frequency for each flagged item, for example weekly, biweekly, or monthly, based on how quickly it seemed to run low, and explain the reasoning for at least two of those frequencies.

resources.title: inventory and restocking worked model
resources.purpose: Shows the starting condition, visible moves, reasoning, and success check before the learner begins.
content: Starting condition: Following a worked example, the learner picks one shared-space category, the pantry shelf, the bathroom toiletries, or the under-sink cleaning supplies, and physically checks what's actually there, comparing it against a simple low, adequate, or full rule to flag what needs restocking.
Model move 1: Read the condition and name the exact inventory and restocking decision or action.
Model move 2: Before counting anything, decide which one category you will inventory: pantry staples, toiletries, or cleaning supplies.
Model move 3: Walk through this modeled example first: a household checks its toiletry shelf and finds 1 bar of soap (low), 3 rolls of toilet paper (adequate), and 0 tubes of toothpaste (out).

Model check: Inventory accuracy: Lists at least six real items with quantities and a low/adequate/full label applied consistently using the stated rule. | Restock reasoning: Names two items to restock first with a specific, plausible reason for the priority order.

resources.title: inventory and restocking action steps
resources.purpose: Provides the ordered directions used by the model, guided attempt, independent task, and retry.
content: 1. Read the goal, constraints, and privacy boundary for inventory and restocking.
2. Analyze the worked model and identify why its sequence meets the criteria.
3. Complete the guided case and use feedback before moving on.
4. Select the permitted real-life route or the complete fictional route.
5. Carry out the task, retaining only the minimum evidence named in the record.
6. Compare the result with the success checks and complete the correction loop when needed.

resources.title: inventory and restocking coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: Following a worked example, the learner picks one shared-space category, the pantry shelf, the bathroom toiletries, or the under-sink cleaning supplies, and physically checks what's actually there, comparing it against a simple low, adequate, or full rule to flag what needs restocking.
Coach direction: Before counting anything, decide which one category you will inventory: pantry staples, toiletries, or cleaning supplies.
Learner prompt: Which category did you choose (pantry staples, toiletries, or cleaning supplies), and why?
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: inventory and restocking complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: Walk through this modeled example first: a household checks its toiletry shelf and finds 1 bar of soap (low), 3 rolls of toilet paper (adequate), and 0 tubes of toothpaste (out). Using the rule 'zero or one of an everyday item counts as low, two to three counts as adequate, four or more counts as full,' the household flags soap and toothpaste for restocking but leaves the toilet paper alone. If a real shared space isn't available, use this sample list instead: canned soup (2 cans), rice (1 bag), pasta (0 boxes), cooking oil (1 bottle), paper towels (3 rolls) — apply the same rule to these five sample items.
Response 1 (t2-p1): I understand the rule: zero-to-one is low, two-to-three is adequate, four-or-more is full.
Response 2 (t2-p2): I applied the rule correctly to the modeled toiletry example above.

Equal-access rule: If a real shared space isn't available to inventory, use the sample pantry/toiletry list provided on this task sheet instead, applying the same low/adequate/full rule to the sample quantities given.

resources.title: inventory and restocking minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.
Reflection: Was the low/adequate/full rule easy to apply to every item, or did any item not fit neatly into one category? Explain.

Success checks: Inventory accuracy: Lists at least six real items with quantities and a low/adequate/full label applied consistently using the stated rule. | Restock reasoning: Names two items to restock first with a specific, plausible reason for the priority order.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: inventory and restocking supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g8-u02-l02-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g8-u02-l02-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional inventory and restocking condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Inventory accuracy: Lists at least six real items with quantities and a low/adequate/full label applied consistently using the stated rule. | Restock reasoning: Names two items to restock first with a specific, plausible reason for the priority order..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g8-u02-l02-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

guardianInvolvement.role: Optional coach only; no guardian attestation is required.
guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.

privacy.rule: Collect the smallest process record that shows the lesson steps. A learner may choose fictional details and may decline private disclosure without losing credit.

account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details
photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules

may: coach the guided and retry cards
mayNot: observe or claim a physical condition
tutorBoundary.physicalCompletionRule: Tutor or AI may coach. Tutor or AI may not certify that a real-world physical action occurred.
tutorBoundary.missingResourceAction: Stop and name the unresolved resource. Do not fabricate it; use another complete delivered route only when every resource for that route resolves.
